versions.localizedDescription:
A performance update for iPhone, plus gyro aiming. Your saves and extracted game data carry over unchanged.

**iPhone & iPad**
- **Smoother and faster:** Hyrule Field now holds a locked 120 fps on a 120 Hz iPhone (it used to swing between about 63 and 110 fps). Music no longer slows down when frames run late, because the game clock keeps real time. The sun's lens flare and light glows no longer stall the game every tick, and moving the touch stick no longer redraws the whole on-screen overlay.
- **Gyro aiming** (off by default, with a sensitivity slider): tilt the device to aim the bow, slingshot, hookshot and first-person view. It does not move the free camera.
- **Always Show Menu Button:** a new option that keeps the menu button on screen during gameplay.
- **Anchor (online co-op):** a warning under Team ID when players in your room are on different teams.

**Apple Vision Pro**
- The light-glow stall fix applies here too, Window mode gets the same music-timing fix, and the Anchor team warning is included.

This public build does not include the developer console; the OTA test builds do.

Built on Ship of Harkinian 9.3.0 (upstream commit ecd889c).
Bring your own ROM; the app extracts it on device.

A fix for touch players: the on-screen **R** button works again. Your saves and extracted
game data carry over unchanged.

**iPhone & iPad**
- **Fix:** the touch **R** button now raises your shield (and does everything else R does)
  with the default controller settings. It used to send a button the default layout
  doesn't use, so tapping it did nothing unless you rebound R by hand. If you already
  rebound R to RB as a workaround, that keeps working too; you can also put it back to
  the default.

**Apple Vision Pro**
- The window's touch R button gets the same fix. Nothing else changes.

This public build does not include the developer console; the OTA test builds do.

Built on Ship of Harkinian 9.3.0 (upstream commit ecd889c).
Bring your own ROM; the app extracts it on device.

Touch players can now steer the camera with a finger: turn on Free Look and drag on any
empty part of the screen to look around. Your saves and extracted game data carry over
unchanged.

**iPhone & iPad**
- **Touch camera:** turn on Free Look in **Settings > Controls > Camera Controls**, then
  drag on empty screen space (anywhere that isn't a button or the stick) to turn the
  camera. Free Look's own sensitivity and invert options apply. A new **Touch Camera
  Sensitivity** slider in **Settings > iOS** sets how far a drag turns; at 1.00, one
  screen width turns the camera 180 degrees. The left-handed layout mirrors the drag
  area too.
- **Fix:** tapping a touch C-button no longer jerks the camera when Free Look is on.
  C-buttons still do everything else they did (C-up still looks in first person), and a
  game controller's right stick still moves the camera as before.

**Apple Vision Pro**
- No changes in this release. Touch drag-look is for iPhone and iPad only.

**Texture packs**
- The pause menu's "C-button to Equip" prompt with HD packs now uses upstream's own fix
  instead of ours. We checked it with the Reloaded 4K pack, and it looks the same as before.

This public build does not include the developer console; the OTA test builds do.

Ship of Harkinian 9.3.0 comes to iPhone and Apple Vision Pro: speedrun mode, a big
randomizer update, boss death skips, instant text and much more. Your existing saves and
extracted game data keep working.

**From upstream Ship of Harkinian 9.3.0**
- **Speedrun mode:** new Speedrun and Speedrun MQ modes with presets made with the OoT
  speedrunning community. Starting a new file now opens a quest select screen.
- **Randomizer shuffles:** signs, butterflies, wonder items, the beggar, icicles, red ice,
  rocks, silver rupees, the treasure chest game, Zelda's letter, the scarecrow song and
  masks. Also progressive Biggoron's Sword, progressive open chests, a logical Bunny Hood,
  and a shop option that holds back shields and tunics until you find one.
- **Randomizer win conditions redesigned:** Triforce pieces can award different rewards,
  win conditions can be tied to different gates, and Ganon's boss soul can be gated
  separately from his boss key.
- **Randomizer starting items** are now a grid of item icons, covering many more items.
- **Boss death skips** for every boss.
- **More cutscene skips**, with more accurate time of day around the intro, Master Sword
  and Sun's Song skips.
- **Instant text** option.
- More minigame settings.
- Better support for large custom audio packs.
- **Enemy randomizer:** adds the Flare Dancer, plus options that stop enemies falling into
  pits.

**Apple Vision Pro**
- No VR-side changes in this release; you get everything above in all three modes.
- The extraction changes listed under iPhone & iPad apply here too.

**iPhone & iPad**
- ROM extraction now uses upstream's new extractor (Torch). It still runs inside the app,
  from your own ROM.
- Game data you extracted with an earlier version keeps working; there is nothing to
  re-extract.
- The app is about 10 MB larger, because it carries the extraction tables for every
  supported ROM version.

This public build does not include the developer console; the OTA test builds do.

Fixes the two 1.1.1 bugs reported in issue #1: the Scarecrow's Song softlock, and
the game coming back stretched after Control Center, a notification or an app
switch. Also fixes building from a fresh clone.

**iPhone & iPad**
- **Scarecrow's Song no longer softlocks.** Recording Bonooru's song or playing
  it for Pierre used to leave the ocarina staff on screen most of the time; an
  ocarina note-timer could wrap under the iOS audio thread's pacing. Thanks to
  GMoxFr for the root cause and the tested fix.
- **No more stretched picture after leaving the app.** Control Center, the
  notification shade, an app switch or lock/unlock brought the game back
  squashed into portrait proportions until a relaunch. The app now re-asserts
  landscape and its window size on every return (built against the iOS 27 SDK,
  which broke the orientation query SDL relied on). LiveContainer users: this
  also fixes the black screen and the stuck-in-portrait cases.
- Building from a fresh clone works again (two overlay patches had lost their
  CRLF bytes in this repo; two shell-script fixes in the audio deps build).

**Apple Vision Pro**
- No VR-facing changes; the visionOS build carries the ocarina fix.

This public build does not include the developer console; the OTA test builds do.

HD texture packs: scrolling water and lava (Death Mountain Crater, Water Temple,
Zora waterfalls) no longer jitter. Built with Xcode 27 / iOS 27 SDK; the iOS
shell now uses the UIScene life cycle.

**iPhone & iPad**
- **HD texture packs no longer make scrolling surfaces jiggle.** With a
  Reloaded-style pack installed, Death Mountain Crater's lava, the Water
  Temple's water and the Zora waterfalls shimmered and jumped; they are steady
  now. Two fixes: tile pixel sizes are rounded instead of truncated, and
  scrolling display lists carry their two endpoints and interpolate at draw
  time instead of baking a fractional size per frame.
- **Built against the iOS 27 SDK**, and the iOS shell has adopted the UIScene
  life cycle that SDK requires — without it the app is killed before it starts.
- Scrolling textures are also cheaper at high interpolation rates, so scroll-
  heavy rooms cost less at 120 Hz.

**Apple Vision Pro**
- No VR-facing changes in this release. The visionOS build carries the same
  scrolling-texture fixes and the Xcode 27 toolchain.

Ocarina of Time in **immersive VR on Apple Vision Pro** — you stand in Hyrule in
first person and swing the sword with your own hand. Tap **VR** in the ornament
under the game window (**3D** and **Exit** are right beside it; the game keeps
running across the switch).

**Apple Vision Pro**
- **Motion combat** — your Sense controllers are your hands, and a real swing
  swings the blade: slashes, stabs and combos come out of how you actually move
- **First-person immersion** — Link's body is hidden, the camera is your head,

- **The item wheel** — hold the right grip and the game's own 3D item models fan
  out around your hand; look at one and let go to equip it
- **Aim with your hand** — bow, slingshot, hookshot and boomerang follow the
  controller's own aim ray, with a crosshair you can always see
- **The Megaton hammer** chops with a wrist flex, and **the Lens of Truth**
  renders as a single fused circle out in the world
- Shield crouch, Z-targeting on the left trigger, ladders, and the HUD floating
  where you can read it
- **Hand calibration and an in-game VR settings sheet**, with a per-section
  Reset so a bad tweak costs one tap

**iPhone & iPad**
- No iPhone-facing changes in this release

Fixes game controller buttons triggering menu actions on iPad — B opened and closed the menu on every press.

First public release of Ship of Harkinian (The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time) for iPhone and Apple Vision Pro — a native Metal port.

**Features**
- Full quest with saves, audio and music, and cutscenes
- The Ship of Harkinian enhancements menu (higher frame rates, widescreen, quality-of-life toggles)
- In-app ROM extraction — no PC tools needed
- Game controllers with menu-aware navigation, plus a tunable on-screen touch layout (including per-button hide/show)
- 60 / 120 Hz (ProMotion) and a supersampling slider
- Texture-pack (`.o2r`) support via drag-and-drop in Files
- **Apple Vision Pro:** a true-4K windowed mode plus a world-locked **stereoscopic 3D mode** with foveated rendering and spatial audio

**Install:** add the SideStore source and install — see the [README](https://github.com/rebelancap/Shipwright-ios#install). Bring your own Ocarina of Time ROM; no game content is included.

versions.localizedDescription:
A performance and controls update for iPhone, plus a launch-crash fix. Your saves and extracted `mm.o2r` carry over unchanged; no re-extraction needed.

**iPhone & iPad**
- **Smoother and faster:** holds a locked 120 fps on a 120 Hz iPhone with an HD texture pack. Music no longer slows down when frames run late, because the game clock keeps real time. Light glows and the sun's lens flare no longer stall the game every tick, and moving the touch stick no longer redraws the whole on-screen overlay.
- **Launch-crash fix:** if your settings had the renderer set to OpenGL (which this app does not include), the game crashed at launch. It now falls back to Metal and repairs the setting by itself. Settings > Graphics > Renderer API lists Metal only.
- **Drag-to-look:** with Free Look on, swipe on empty screen space to move the camera (sensitivity slider in the iOS settings). Holding a touch C-button no longer swings the camera.
- **Gyro aiming** (off by default, with a sensitivity slider): tilt the phone to aim the bow, hookshot and first-person view.
- **Always Show Menu Button:** a new option that keeps the menu button on screen during gameplay.
- **iOS settings section restored:** 1.1.0 and 1.1.1 accidentally shipped a cut-down version of it. Double-Tap Z, Haptics, Opacity, Left-Handed, Stick Response, Customize Layout, Max Frame Rate, Supersampling and the Performance HUD are back in the menu.
- The touch R button now acts as the right trigger.
- Built with the iOS 27 SDK: launches correctly and stays landscape on iOS 27.

**Apple Vision Pro**
- The light-glow stall fix, the music-timing fix and the launch-crash fix apply here too. Verified on the visionOS simulator; this build was not tested in the headset (visionOS unworn in the headset), and the 3D mode is unchanged from 1.1.1.

This public build does not include the developer console.

Built on 2 Ship 2 Harkinian 5.0.1 "Battler Bravo".

Folds in upstream **2 Ship 2 Harkinian 5.0.1 "Battler Bravo"**.

**Your existing `mm.o2r` and save files carry over.** Unlike 1.1.0, this
update does *not* require re-extracting from your ROM — 5.0.1 keeps the
same archive format major version.

### Upstream fixes in 5.0.1

- Song of Time now returns Link to the file select properly
- Owl Statue saving skips to the file select
- Save delay is allowed when voiding out during an owl save
- Pause-buffer input fix: no more pause loop when pausing to save
- The moon-crash cutscene is no longer skipped when attempting the 4th-day glitch
- The aliens cutscene is no longer skipped while Sun's Song is active
- Shrine feathers no longer despawn when voiding out
- Blast mask check no longer granted for killing/ignoring Sakon
- Frame interpolation fixed for archery-minigame enemies and bubbles
- `masksGivenOnMoon` is reset on file load
- Two item-tracker quirks fixed; tracker handles incremented events; small Snowhead logic tweak
- Tingle map & Bomber's Notebook checks are re-obtainable again
- Time Moves When You Move: fixes saving a zero time speed
- Incompatible `.o2r` archives are now removed properly across app directories
- Fixes a crash when opening the menu while regenerating an OTR

### iOS / visionOS port

No port-side changes this release beyond the version bump — the iOS shell,
touch layout, controller support, and visionOS 3D mode are unchanged from 1.1.0.

Folds in Harbour Masters' **5.0.0 "Battler Alfa"**, a large upstream release —
so this one is a minor bump rather than the usual patch.

> ### ⚠️ You must re-extract your ROM after updating
>
> 5.0.0 changes the game-archive format, so the `mm.o2r` produced by any
> earlier version is no longer accepted. On first launch you'll see
> **"Outdated ROM Archives"** and be sent back to the extractor — point it at
> your Majora's Mask ROM again and it will rebuild the archive. This is
> expected, it is not a broken build, and it applies to everyone upgrading.
>
> **Your save files are not affected.** Saves and settings carry over; only the
> extracted game archive has to be regenerated.

Everything below is upstream's work, now available on iPhone, iPad and Apple
Vision Pro.

### New in the game

- **File setup** — pick Vanilla or Randomizer right from an empty file slot,
  with preset and seed selection on the file select screen.
- **Gameplay** — Bomb Arrows; songs equippable to C/D-Pad buttons and played
  without note input; put masks on straight from the pause menu with A; Fierce
  Deity can use transformation masks; faster bottles; Picto Box on C-Up; custom
  ocarina controls; extra Powder Kegs; infinite Epona carrots; boss health
  multiplier; free look while climbing.
- **Mirrored World** is now a dropdown — Always, Random per scene, Random
  (Seeded), or various dungeon-only modes — plus a fix for Inverted Stone Tower.
- **Time savers** — more skippable one-point cutscenes (Owl Statue, Laundry Pool
  bell) and misc interactions (Kafei, Sakon's hideout, Couple's Mask).
- **Accessibility** — No Random Drops, No Heart Drops, Disable Final Day Quakes,
  an easier Treasure Chest Shop maze view, and a menu background opacity slider.
- **Restorations** — re-bottle soil patch bugs, and the original longer day
  transition card.
- **Cosmetics & mods** — the SoH Cosmetics Editor and Mod menu, a dynamic
  cosmetics editor for custom models, trail colors, XML skeleton support, and
  alt toggles for custom models/skeletons/animations.
- **Audio** — basic surround sound support, and song categories so randomized
  sequences are matched by category.
- **Randomizer** — new shuffles (butterflies, beehives, wonder items, skeleton
  key, Tycoon's Wallet), reworked Gold Skulltula and dungeon item options, a
  Gossip Stone hint strength slider, new hint types, and a menu overhaul.

Upstream's full notes:
https://github.com/HarbourMasters/2ship2harkinian/releases/tag/5.0.0

### iOS / visionOS side

The port's own layer was rebased onto the new engine — 40 patches over upstream,
covering the Metal path, touch controls, the iOS settings section, the stereo 3D
mode on Vision Pro, and the audio/CVar thread-safety fixes. Two notes:

- **One workaround retired as fixed upstream.** This port carried a patch to
  stop the cosmetic scan reading every file in every installed texture pack at
  boot — on a 4K pack that meant a long black screen. 5.0.0 replaces that scan
  with a manifest, so only the materials a pack actually declares are loaded,
  and the workaround was dropped rather than carried forward.
- **The audio-thread crash guard was kept.** 5.0.0 added its own null checks
  there, but they don't cover the case this port hit, so the existing fix stays.

No changes to touch layout, controller bindings, or the 3D mode in this release.

versions.localizedDescription:
An iOS 27 compatibility, performance and stability update. Your saves and extracted `sf64.o2r` carry over unchanged; no re-extraction needed.

**iPhone & iPad**
- **Built with the iOS 27 SDK:** the app launches correctly on iOS 27 and stays in landscape. Previously the game could end up laid out in portrait (squeezed into a column) on a landscape screen. Returning from the Home screen resumes the game instead of leaving a black screen.
- **Game speed holds real time:** when a frame runs late, the game now catches up instead of slowing down, so stages, enemies and the Arwing no longer drift into slow motion on a busy frame.
- **Smoother touch controls:** moving the on-screen stick or holding Z no longer redraws the whole touch overlay every frame, which removes stutter while steering with touch.
- **Always Show Menu Button:** a new option (Settings > iOS > Menu) that keeps the menu button on screen during gameplay instead of only on the title screen and while paused.
- **Launch-crash fix:** if your settings had the renderer set to OpenGL (which this app does not include), the game crashed at launch. It now falls back to Metal and repairs the setting by itself.
- Still includes the 1.0.1 controller fix: on iPad, a game controller's B button no longer opens and closes the menu on every press.

**Apple Vision Pro**
- The game-speed fix, the touch overlay improvement and the launch-crash fix apply to the window mode too. Verified on the visionOS simulator; this build was not tested in the headset, and the 3D mode is unchanged from 1.0.1.

versions.localizedDescription:
# SpaghettiKart for iPhone & Apple Vision Pro — 1.1.0

## New: VR mode on Apple Vision Pro

Mario Kart 64, fully immersive. Alongside the existing 2D window and 3D panel, VR mode puts the race all around you:

- **Three ways to race:** **first person** from the driver's seat, **third person** from beside your kart, or **Diorama** — the whole track as a tabletop model in front of you.
- **Rear-view panes:** one floating above the HUD, and one on your left hand when you hold a PlayStation VR2 Sense controller. Click the left stick (on a Sense controller or a gamepad) to toggle the top pane.
- **HUD row** with live-adjustable height, so the race info sits where you like it.
- **A world-locked sky:** clouds and stars stay put in the world as you turn and tilt your head, in both eyes.
- **Controllers:** gamepads and PlayStation VR2 Sense controllers both drive the game.
- **Recenter / Recalculate height** button to snap the view back to the seat.
- **Smooth at speed:** the view follows the game's frame interpolation, so other karts, shadows and boost effects no longer double up or jitter while you drive.
- **No rainbow flashes:** the occasional single-eye rainbow flash is gone, and the jumbotron screens stay live in VR.

## iPhone & iPad

- **Built for iOS 27:** launches on current iOS and stays in landscape after Home or Control Center.
- **Game speed holds real time under load** — races no longer slow down when the frame rate dips.
- **Jumbotron / TV screens no longer stall the GPU** every frame.
- **Lighter touch controls:** the on-screen controls cost far less to draw.
- **Centered "ROM needed" prompt** on first launch, on every phone and orientation.
- **Launch-crash guard:** picking an unsupported renderer (OpenGL) in Settings → Graphics can no longer stop the app from launching; it falls back to Metal.
- **Always Show Menu Button** option for the on-screen menu button.

## Also

- HUD and settings polish across both platforms.
- Lakitu sits closer and higher at the start line in VR first person.
- Left-stick click toggles the rear view in VR on gamepads as well as Sense controllers.

## Install

Add a SideStore / AltStore source (*Sources → + → paste the URL*) — the app updates itself from there:

| Device | Source | Source URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone / iPad | HarbourMasters ports | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebelancap/harbourmasters-ports/main/apps-ios.json` |
| iPhone / iPad | All ports | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebelancap/all-ports/main/apps-ios.json` |
| Apple Vision Pro | HarbourMasters ports | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebelancap/harbourmasters-ports/main/apps-visionos.json` |
| Apple Vision Pro | All ports | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebelancap/all-ports/main/apps-visionos.json` |

Or download `spaghettikart-1.1.0-iOS.ipa` / `spaghettikart-1.1.0-visionOS.ipa` below and sideload it. Bring your own Mario Kart 64 ROM; no game content is included.

versions.localizedDescription:
A fix for the repeating "Outdated ROM Archives" popup, smoother game timing and touch controls, and an iOS 27 rebuild.

**If you are upgrading from 1.0.x**
- **"Outdated ROM Archives" popup fixed:** archives made by 1.0.x showed this popup at every launch, and pressing OK went straight into the game without re-extracting anything. You will now see the popup **once**: confirm the prompts and the app re-extracts `bk.o2r` from the ROM in your Lighthouse folder (about half a minute), then later launches are silent. Your old archive is set aside and only removed once the new one checks out. If your ROM is no longer in the Lighthouse folder, the file picker opens so you can choose it again. Saves are untouched. Archives already made by 1.1.0 are current and launch without the popup.

**iPhone & iPad**
- **Game keeps real time:** when a frame runs late, the game now skips an in-between frame instead of slowing down, so movement and music no longer drift into slow motion.
- **Lighter touch controls:** the on-screen stick no longer redraws the whole overlay as you move it, cutting the per-frame work the touch layer costs.
- **Launch-crash fix:** if your settings had the renderer set to OpenGL (which this app does not include), the game crashed at launch. It now falls back to Metal and repairs the setting by itself.
- Built with the iOS 27 SDK: launches correctly on iOS 27 and stays landscape, including after returning from Home or Control Center.

**Apple Vision Pro**
- The archive-popup fix, the launch-crash fix, the real-time timing (2D mode) and the lighter touch overlay apply here too. Verified on the visionOS simulator; this build was not tested in the headset, and the 3D mode is unchanged from 1.1.0.

This public build does not include the developer console.

Built on Lighthouse 1.1.0 "Hatteras Alfa".
Bring your own Banjo-Kazooie ROM (`.z64`, US v1.0, US v1.1, Japan or PAL); the app extracts it on device and ships no game content.

## Install

| Device | Source URL |
| --- | --- |
| iPhone / iPad | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebelancap/harbourmasters-ports/main/apps-ios.json` |
| Apple Vision Pro | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebelancap/harbourmasters-ports/main/apps-visionos.json` |

Or install the IPA below manually through SideStore/AltStore (iPhone can also use Sideloadly).

## Internal Resolution is now pinned at 100%

*Settings → Graphics → Internal Resolution* is greyed out and reads 100%.

It never did anything on iPhone or Apple Vision Pro. The multiplier feeds one consumer, and this port's supersampling pass recomputes the same values from the native drawable size — so the multiplier cancels out and is divided straight back out. On Vision Pro's stereoscopic path it is skipped entirely. A slider that visibly does nothing is worse than no slider, so it now says so and points you at the control that does work:

| Device | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| iPhone | **Supersampling** — *Settings → iOS* |
| Apple Vision Pro | **Render Scale** — *Settings → iOS* (oversampling is automatic) |

Nothing about how the game actually renders has changed — it was already at full native resolution.

## On the iOS side

The overlay is now 45 patches, down from 46: the `argv[argc]` null-dereference fix (a crash on any argument-bearing launch) was **retired** because upstream fixed it independently.

One patch needed real work. Upstream moved the audio-init call into the engine constructor, which left the port's audio-rate helper defined *below* its only caller. Every overlay integrity check still passed — the patch applied, reversed and regenerated cleanly — while the tree no longer compiled. A good reminder that the drill is not a build.

## What's in it

- The full adventure — every world, with saves, audio, music and cutscenes
- The **Lighthouse enhancements menu** — higher frame rates, widescreen, and the quality-of-life catalogue
- The **randomizer** and **online co-op (Anchor)**
- **ROM-hack support** — extract a Banjo's Backpack hack on the device and it installs as a mod overlay
- **In-app ROM extraction** — Torch compiled in, runs in-process
- **Game controllers** with menu-aware navigation, and touch controls built for an N64 platformer: floating analog stick, the four C-buttons, Z with an optional double-tap hold, and a layout customizer with per-button hide/show
- **Hold A to fast-forward dialog**
- **60 / 120 Hz** (ProMotion) and a supersampling slider
- Texture packs and other `.o2r` mods via drag-and-drop in Files
- **Apple Vision Pro:** a freely resizable 2D window rendering at true 4K, plus a **stereoscopic 3D mode** — the game on a world-locked panel in your room, with foveated rendering, spatial audio anchored to the screen, and live-tunable depth, size, distance and height

## Requirements

- iPhone on **iOS 15+**, or **Apple Vision Pro** (visionOS 2+)
- Your own Banjo-Kazooie ROM (`.z64`) — US v1.0, US v1.1, Japan or PAL
- SideStore, installed with [iloader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader) (Vision Pro needs the [visionOS fork](https://github.com/rebelancap/iloader/releases#release-visionos) and an Apple Silicon Mac)

## Notes

- ROM hacks are **extended ROMs** (larger than a 16 MB retail dump) and are built against **US v1.0** — extraction works from any base, but playing a hack correctly needs a `bk.o2r` made from a US v1.0 ROM. The app tells you if your base is the wrong version.
- Banjo-Kazooie's model textures are currently bundled into the model data rather than addressed individually, so texture packs reach less of the world than the equivalent packs do in the other ports. That's an upstream limitation.
